tig.why: Infobox gives ~1.0M (Ethnologue 2022-2024); ours (1.3) was too high, no L1/L2 split available so total matches l1.

ln.why: Infobox nation field lists Lingala as national language in both DR Congo and Republic of the Congo; ours was missing Republic of the Congo.

xh.why: Wikidata official_in and infobox both list Zimbabwe (one of its 16 official languages) in addition to South Africa.

wo.why: Infobox (2022-2023) gives L1 8.2M / total 18M, notably higher than ours; infobox nation field also gives Wolof national-language status in Senegal.

ee.why: Infobox gives ~5.0M (2013-2019), well below ours (7); no L1/L2 split so l1=total.

tn.why: Wikidata official_in and infobox nation field both add Zimbabwe (Setswana is one of Zimbabwe's 16 official languages).

ss.why: Infobox gives L1 2.3M + L2 2.4M (2013) = ~4.7M total, well above ours (3.0); l1 (2.5) stayed within tolerance.

ny.why: Wikidata official_in lists Malawi and Zimbabwe (Chewa is one of Zimbabwe's 16 official languages), not Zambia (which only has regional/lingua-franca status, not national official).

zh.why: official_by_label for the Standard Chinese / Standard Taiwanese Mandarin variants adds Hong Kong and Macao alongside China, Taiwan, Singapore.

nan.why: Wiktionary gives 再會 (chài-hoē) as the native Hokkien goodbye; ours mixed the Mandarin character/reading 再見 (kiàn) which isn't a real Hokkien pronunciation.

lo.why: Infobox gives L1 3.7M + L2 0.8M = ~4.5M (2015), vs ours 30/30 which was off by 6-7x -- likely conflated with Isan/Lao speakers in Thailand.

su.why: Wikivoyage lists Sampurasun as the standard greeting and Halo only as the informal variant; ours had the informal form as primary.

ms.unsure: Ours (l1 20 / total 80) is far below the infobox/Wikidata figures (L1 ~90M, L2 ~180M), but those appear to be macrolanguage-wide figures that fold in Indonesian speakers; ours seems to deliberately scope Malay to Malaysia/Brunei/Singapore. Left unchanged, flagging for human review.

pa.why: wikidata_official_in is empty and infobox nation field only lists India + its states/regional additional status; like Tamil/Kannada/Maithili, Punjabi is a scheduled/regional language in India, not official at the national level (Pakistan only gives it provincial status).

fa.why: Infobox combined Farsi+Dari+Tajik L1 figure is ~91M (our total of 130 already matched the infobox's combined total of ~127M well, but l1=70 was >20% below the infobox L1).

tr.why: Wikidata official_in and infobox nation field both add Northern Cyprus alongside Turkey and Cyprus.

ug.why: Wiktionary and Wikivoyage both spell thanks with ھ (rehmet); ours used خ (rakhmat), a misspelling/confusion with the Kazakh/Uzbek form.

bo.unsure: Bye phrase (ཕྱིས་འཇལ / Chi jal) doesn't match either Wiktionary (ག་ལེ་ཕེབས/ག་ལེ་ཞུགས) or Wikivoyage (kha lay shug/pheb); couldn't confidently verify the correct Tibetan script for a replacement, flagging for human review.

pt.why: Wikidata official_in and infobox both add Equatorial Guinea and Macao alongside the 8 countries ours already had.

hr.why: Infobox's own footnote says Bosnia and Herzegovina has no state-level official language (Croatian is only official in its sub-national entities, which doesn't count); Wikidata official_in and infobox both add Montenegro (co-official nationally) instead.

lt.why: Wikidata and infobox both agree on 4.0M total speakers (vs ours 3); l1 (2.8) stayed within tolerance of Lithuania's resident native-speaker population.

fi.why: Wikidata official_in adds Sweden, where Finnish has official minority-language status nationally.

da.why: Wikidata official_in only lists Denmark and the Faroe Islands; the infobox puts Greenland under 'minority', not 'nation' (Greenlandic, not Danish, is Greenland's official language).

br.why: Wikidata's current (2025, preferred) and infobox (2024) figures both give ~107,000 speakers, well below ours (160,000); total (0.21) kept as a plausible broader L1+L2 estimate.

gl.why: Wikidata official_in lists Spain (Galician is co-official, like Catalan/Basque); ours had no official status at all.

nah.why: Wikidata official_in lists Mexico; Nahuatl has national-language status under Mexico's 2003 General Law of Linguistic Rights of Indigenous Peoples, alongside Spanish.
nah.unsure: Bye phrase (Mocheli) doesn't match Wiktionary's 'anej', but Nahuatl has huge dialectal variation and no Wikivoyage data to arbitrate; left phrase unchanged, flagging for human review.

sm.why: Infobox (430,440, 2020-2022) and all Wikidata figures cluster around 0.41-0.43M; ours (0.51) was consistently ~20% above every reference.
